blocks.en:
anyway. merlin is ready to work. I'm still figuring out the right
balance of skills and workflow, but the foundation is there. feels like
I gave an old machine a soul. kinda poetic, if you think about it.

but here's the thing that actually blew my mind --- the mimo voice
models. I've been playing with them all day and they are *excellent*.
like, actually excellent. not "good for a free model" excellent. just.
excellent. the voice design stuff lets you describe a voice and it
generates it from scratch. I have been a xiaomi fan for the last 8
years, and I swear, nobody talks about them enough. these people are
driving innovation like no other company on the planet and I will die on
this hill.

configured the whole thing with mimo 2.5 as the main driver, and
honestly, it just works. the whole setup was smoother than I expected
for a machine that was probably designed to run solitaire and nothing
else (Okay I'm exagerating). gave the bot a name too. **merlin vieira
saar**. yes, that's my bot. yes, I'm proud of it. don't judge me.

ok, so today was wild. pulled out this ancient HP pavilion from god
knows where --- the thing has seen better days, let me tell you --- and
decided to set up a full Hermes agent on it. because why not. every
laptop deserves a second life.

the whole experience made me think about how weird and beautiful this
moment is. I'm sitting here, talking to a bot named merlin, running on a
laptop that's older than some of my students, using voice tech from a
company that most people in the west still associate with budget phones.
meanwhile, the actual product is lightyears ahead of what the "premium"
brands are shipping.
